findings.title: Model sanitizer does not handle the real `claude-opus-4-6[1m]` suffix from the issue.
findings.body:
The issue shows Claude Code sending `"model": "claude-opus-4-6[1m]"`, a literal bracketed suffix with a closing `]`. The fallback regex `/\[[0-9;]*m$/i` only matches a trailing `[1m` with no closing bracket, so this value passes through unchanged as `gen_ai.request.model`.

Model and pricing lookups keyed on `claude-opus-4-6` will then miss, and cost and model analytics for these spans come out wrong. The test only covers the ESC-prefixed form `\u001b[1m`.

Fix: also strip a trailing `\[[0-9;]*m\]?$`, or decide on purpose how to map the `[1m]` context-size marker. Add a fixture with the literal value from the issue.

findings.title: Any span with a `span.type` attribute is now exported, whatever its value.
findings.body:
The default export predicate now returns true for any span that has a `span.type` key. `span.type` is a generic attribute: Datadog-style and other instrumentations set it to values like `web`, `db`, `http` or `cache`. Those ordinary HTTP and DB spans will now pass the smart filter and be exported to Latitude. That defeats the filter's purpose and adds noise and ingest cost.

Fix: only match when the value is a Claude Code type, for example `span.attributes["span.type"] === "interaction" || === "llm_request"`. Keep the `user_prompt` and `llm_request.context` checks as they are.
